items.title: AI大廠搶設備搶到缺貨！艾司摩爾連兩年擴產仍不夠
items.title_en: AI Giant Scrambles for Equipment, Still Faces Shortages! ASML Expands Production for Two Years Yet Still Insufficient
paras: AI晶片需求旺盛，艾司摩爾(ASML-US)卻面臨設備供應追不上客戶擴產的挑戰。執行長福克(Christophe Fouquet)坦言，用於製造先進邏輯與記憶體晶片的微影設備，2027年與2028年的供應都將不足以滿足需求。投資人關注的焦點，也從訂單是否充足，轉向公司能否及時增加產能，把需求轉化為獲利。
據《路透》報導，福克今年4月才向股東承諾，將「盡一切可能」避免艾司摩爾成為晶片產業的瓶頸。如今，這家歐洲市值最高的公司雖然訂單需求強勁，卻也面臨AI投資能否持續、遠期成長預測是否過於樂觀的市場質疑。

連兩年擴產仍不夠 設備供應成成長關卡

持有艾司摩爾股票的財富管理公司Aureus投資長迪佩林克(Han Dieperink)表示：「艾司摩爾本身現在就是瓶頸。」他指出，管理層已公開承認，即使2027年與2028年各增加30%產能，仍不足以滿足需求。
客戶對未來訂單的討論，甚至已延伸至2029年與2030年。迪佩林克認為，這顯示供不應求的情況可能延續至本輪景氣循環之後。
為提高交付能力，艾司摩爾正設法縮短組裝時間、升級客戶已在使用的設備，並推出生產速度更快的新機型。公司原先計畫到2028年，將單價約2億美元的極紫外光(EUV)微影設備年產能提高至110台，如今正考慮再增加約12台。
艾司摩爾也在恩荷芬擴建製造產能，但第一階段預計要到2029年才會啟用。福克周三則強調，包括關鍵光學系統供應商蔡司(Zeiss)在內，艾司摩爾自身的供應鏈並非目前的限制因素。
除了增加出貨，公司也表示，2027年與2028年的價格調漲將有助業績成長。

需求強勁未消估值疑慮 AI融資與回報受檢驗

艾司摩爾股價今年以來已上漲近70%，但市場對2028年之後的前景愈來愈謹慎。自6月以來，儘管分析師持續上修獲利預估，股價相對於未來獲利的估值卻逐步下降。
Stonehage Fleming資深分析師史隆(Mark Sloan)指出，艾司摩爾預估本益比已從6月的逾45倍降至約30倍。考量成長前景與市場主導地位，他認為目前估值具有吸引力。該公司旗下Global Best Ideas基金約有3.5%的部位配置於艾司摩爾。
史隆表示，團隊正密切追蹤AI普及、技術創新，以及主要客戶的資本支出計畫，並認為未來限制艾司摩爾成長的關鍵，仍較可能是供給而非需求。
不過，部分投資人質疑，龐大的AI基礎設施支出，最終能否創造足以支撐投資的回報。高利率也可能提高大型AI與資料中心專案的融資難度，美國科技業違約保障成本周四已升至歷史新高。
Jefferies分析師梅農(Janardan Menon)指出，AI投資融資疑慮，以及電力供應等資料中心擴張限制，都可能拖累艾司摩爾。他認為，市場對2028年與2029年高成長預期的懷疑，是估值下修的主要原因；若進入下行期，本益比可能降至20倍出頭。艾司摩爾盤中股價周四隨大盤賣壓下跌5%。

大額預付款防撤單 遠期訂單暫不急著收

客戶仍積極爭取艾司摩爾先進設備的供應名額，公司則要求支付大額預付款。財務長達森(Roger Dassen)形容，金額大到足以讓客戶日後若想取消訂單，會感到「肉痛」。
最大客戶台積電(2330-TW)(TSM-US)替輝達(NVDA-US)與蘋果(AAPL-US)製造晶片，7月曾表示，不預期設備供應會限制擴產，並在周四維持2026年600億至640億美元的資本支出計畫。三星電子(005930-KR)、SK海力士(SKHY-US)與美光(MU-US)，也因AI記憶體需求強勁，積極預訂艾司摩爾產能。
潛在新客戶可能進一步加重供應壓力。馬斯克提出的TeraFab計畫雖尚未生產第一顆晶片，未來仍可能成為先進設備的重要買家。另一方面，美國對中國的出口限制，持續構成艾司摩爾中階深紫外光(DUV)設備銷售風險；中國今年預計占公司營收約20%。
儘管需求強勁，艾司摩爾目前仍暫緩接受2029年與2030年的訂單，以評估客戶準備程度，以及自身滿足未來需求的能力。
達森表示，公司不希望現在先接受部分客戶訂單，之後卻只能告訴尚未下單的其他客戶：「抱歉，我們已經賣光了。」
paras_en: AI chip demand is booming, but ASML (ASML-US) faces the challenge that equipment supply cannot keep up with customers' expansion plans. CEO Christophe Fouquet admitted that lithography equipment used to make advanced logic and memory chips will be insufficient in 2027 and 2028 to meet demand. Investors’ focus has shifted from whether orders are ample to whether the company can increase capacity in time and turn demand into profit.

According to Reuters, Fouquet only promised shareholders in April this year that ASML would "do everything possible" to avoid becoming a bottleneck in the chip industry. Now, despite strong order demand, the Europe‑based market‑cap leader also faces market scepticism over whether AI investment can be sustained and whether long‑term growth forecasts are overly optimistic.

Even after two years of capacity expansion, equipment supply remains a growth hurdle. Han Dieperink, CIO of wealth‑management firm Aureus, which holds ASML stock, said: "ASML itself is now the bottleneck." He noted that management has publicly acknowledged that even a 30% capacity increase in both 2027 and 2028 would still fall short of demand.
Customers’ discussions about future orders have already stretched out to 2029 and 2030. Dieperink believes this shows that the shortage could persist beyond the current economic cycle.

To improve delivery capability, ASML is trying to shorten assembly time, upgrade equipment already in use by customers, and launch faster new models. The company originally planned to raise annual output of its roughly $200 million EUV lithography machines to 110 units by 2028, and is now considering adding about 12 more units.

ASML is also expanding manufacturing capacity in Enschede, but the first phase is not expected to be operational until 2029. Fouquet emphasized on Wednesday that ASML’s own supply chain, including key optics supplier Zeiss, is not the current limiting factor.
In addition to increasing shipments, the company said price hikes in 2027 and 2028 will help drive earnings growth.

Strong demand has not erased valuation concerns; AI financing and returns are under scrutiny. ASML’s share price has risen nearly 70% year‑to‑date, but the market is becoming increasingly cautious about the outlook after 2028. Since June, despite analysts repeatedly raising profit forecasts, the stock’s valuation relative to future earnings has been gradually falling.

Stonehage Fleming senior analyst Mark Sloan noted that ASML’s forward P/E has dropped from over 45× in June to about 30× now. Given its growth prospects and market leadership, he believes the current valuation is attractive. The firm’s Global Best Ideas fund holds roughly a 3.5% position in ASML.

Sloan said his team is closely tracking AI adoption, technological innovation, and major customers’ cap‑ex plans, and believes the key constraint on ASML’s growth will likely remain supply rather than demand.

However, some investors question whether massive AI infrastructure spending will ultimately generate enough return to justify the investment. High interest rates could also raise financing difficulty for large AI and data‑center projects, and U.S. tech‑sector default‑protection costs rose to a historic high on Thursday.

Jefferies analyst Janardan Menon pointed out that concerns over AI investment financing, as well as power‑supply constraints for data‑center expansion, could weigh on ASML. He believes market doubts about the high‑growth expectations for 2028‑29 are the main driver of the valuation downgrade; if a downturn occurs, the P/E could fall to just above 20×. ASML’s intraday price fell 5% on Thursday as the broader market sold off.

Large advance payments to prevent order cancellations – long‑term orders not rushed. Customers are still aggressively seeking slots for ASML’s advanced equipment, and the company requires sizable advance payments. CFO Roger Dassen described the amounts as large enough that customers would feel “pain” if they later tried to cancel an order.

ASML’s biggest customer, TSMC (2330‑TW, TSM‑US), which makes chips for Nvidia (NVDA‑US) and Apple (AAPL‑US), said in July it does not expect equipment supply to limit expansion and maintained its 2026 capital‑expenditure plan of $60‑64 billion on Thursday. Samsung Electronics (005930‑KR), SK Hynix (SKHY‑US) and Micron (MU‑US) are also aggressively booking ASML capacity due to strong AI memory demand.

Potential new customers could further strain supply. Elon Musk’s proposed TeraFab project, although it has not yet produced a chip, could become a major buyer of advanced equipment in the future. Meanwhile, U.S. export restrictions on China continue to pose a sales risk for ASML’s mid‑range DUV equipment; China is expected to account for about 20% of the company’s revenue this year.
Despite strong demand, ASML is temporarily pausing acceptance of orders for 2029 and 2030 to assess customers’ readiness and its own ability to meet future demand.
Dassen said the company does not want to accept some customers’ orders now only to later have to tell other, not‑yet‑ordered customers: “Sorry, we’re sold out.”

items.title: 4天市值蒸發逾百億美元！德銀卻說CoreWeave可以買 看好訂單撐腰
items.title_en: Over $100 Billion Market‑Cap Wiped Out in Four Days, Yet Deutsche Bank Says CoreWeave Is a Buy Backed by Strong Order Flow
paras: CoreWeave(CRWV-US)股債連日遭拋售，短短4個交易日市值蒸發逾100億美元，德意志銀行(DB-US)卻認為，這波跌勢提供了「買進機會」。該行指出，目前難以找到足以合理解釋近期跌幅的公司個別因素，市場可能低估了CoreWeave的客戶基礎、訂單執行能力與基礎設施表現。
CoreWeave信用狀況惡化，引發投資人疑慮，股價本周以來已下跌逾22%。周四(15日)早盤，隨著信用風險指標攀上歷史新高、高收益債券延續跌勢，股價一度再挫9.5%。公司債券周三已跌至通常被視為反映財務困境的價位。
德意志銀行分析師澤尼克(Brad Zelnick)周四在客戶報告中表示，過去一周，多項因素交互作用，似乎導致CoreWeave股票與債券遭到大幅拋售。不過，他坦言：「我們很難找到足以合理解釋近期走勢的公司個別因素。」
維持CoreWeave「買進」評等的澤尼克認為，市場低估了公司的強大客戶基礎、既有執行紀錄、將積壓訂單轉化為營收的能力，以及領先的基礎設施效能。雖然CoreWeave仍須籌措更多資金，但他認為，公司可在龐大客戶訂單支持下，按穩定步調進行融資。
輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳同日也出面力挺，表示CoreWeave的「資金成本實際上正在下降」，而且公司「實力每天都在改善」，因此不需要輝達提供財務後盾。這番談話帶動CoreWeave股價收復部分跌幅。
不過，研究機構顧能(Gartner)(IT-US)對整體產業提出不同警訊，認為AI基礎設施投資熱潮，可能已超前支撐這些投資所需的營收成長。該機構估計，到2030年，逾3.5兆美元的相關支出可能面臨資產減損風險。
顧能並預測，在成本壓力與服務差異化有限的情況下，到2030年，超過八成的新興AI雲端業者將無法繼續獨立營運。這不等同於全部倒閉，但凸顯產業未來可能面臨整併與營運模式調整。
顧能指出，CoreWeave與Nebius(NBIS-US)這類公司的商業模式，更直接繫於市場對運算產能的需求，因此風險尤其突出。Nebius周四午盤下跌5.4%，過去4個交易日累計跌幅達20%，顯示投資人對AI算力供應商的疑慮仍未消退。
paras_en: CoreWeave (CRWV‑US) shares and bonds have been sold off for several days, erasing more than $100 billion of market value in just four trading sessions, but Deutsche Bank (DB‑US) says the decline presents a “buying opportunity.” The bank notes that it is hard to pinpoint any company‑specific factor that would reasonably explain the recent drop, and the market may be undervaluing CoreWeave’s customer base, order‑execution capability, and infrastructure performance.

CoreWeave’s credit profile has deteriorated, raising investor concerns, and the stock has fallen more than 22% so far this week. On Thursday the 15th, early trading saw the credit‑risk metric hit a historic high and high‑yield bonds continue to slide, pushing the share price down another 9.5% at one point. The company’s bonds fell on Wednesday to levels typically viewed as a sign of financial distress.

Deutsche Bank analyst Brad Zelnick wrote in a client note on Thursday that a combination of factors over the past week appears to have driven a sharp sell‑off in CoreWeave’s equity and debt. However, he admitted, “We find it difficult to identify any company‑specific factor that can reasonably explain the recent move.”

Maintaining a “Buy” rating, Zelnick believes the market is underestimating the company’s strong customer base, proven execution record, ability to convert a backlog of orders into revenue, and leading‑edge infrastructure efficiency. While CoreWeave still needs to raise additional capital, he thinks the firm can finance itself at a steady pace supported by its sizable customer orders.

NVIDIA (NVDA‑US) CEO Jensen Huang also weighed in on the same day, saying CoreWeave’s “cost of capital is actually going down” and that the company’s “strength is improving every day,” so it does not need financial backing from NVIDIA. His comments helped the stock recover part of its losses.

However, research firm Gartner (IT‑US) issued a contrasting warning for the broader industry, suggesting that the AI‑infrastructure investment boom may be outpacing the revenue growth needed to sustain those investments. Gartner estimates that by 2030 more than $3.5 trillion of related spending could face asset‑impairment risk.

Gartner also forecasts that, under cost pressure and limited service differentiation, over 80% of emerging AI cloud providers will be unable to continue operating independently by 2030. This does not mean total collapse, but highlights the likelihood of consolidation and business‑model adjustments in the sector.

Gartner points out that companies like CoreWeave and Nebius (NBIS‑US) have business models that are more directly tied to market demand for compute capacity, making their risk profile especially pronounced. Nebius fell 5.4% in early afternoon trading on Thursday, and has dropped a cumulative 20% over the past four trading days, indicating that investor concerns about AI‑compute suppliers remain unresolved.

items.title: 為「親兒子」背書！黃仁勳：CoreWeave財務狀況改善  輝達沒必要提供額外支援
items.title_en: Backing the ‘Favorite Son’: Jensen Huang Says CoreWeave’s Finances Are Improving and Nvidia Need Not Provide Extra Support
paras: AI晶片巨擘輝達的執行長黃仁勳最新表示，CoreWeave財務狀況正在改善，並認為輝達沒必要為CoreWeave提供支援。此前，信貸市場對CoreWeave的態度轉趨負面、認為該公司違約風險正在上升且機率飆破五成。輝達是CoreWeave第二大股東，持股約10%。
黃仁勳週四(15日)在瑞典斯德哥爾摩出席活動時說：「我很樂觀。他們的資本成本實際上正在下降。」他正試圖提振外界對這家資料中心營運商的信心。
CoreWeave是檢驗一批新興企業商業模式能否成立的重要案例。這些企業應運而生，以滿足輝達等公司所稱近乎無止境的AI算力需求。
CoreWeave等公司在包括輝達在內的供應商支持下大量舉債，引發了市場對於「循環融資」的擔憂，認為這種融資模式可能製造虛假需求。
今年1月，輝達宣布深化與CoreWeave合作，該合作包含輝達向CoreWeave投資20億美元，CoreWeave則承諾，到2030年，將採用輝達技術建設超過5GW算力的資料中心。
目前輝達持有CoreWeave 4720萬股股份，持股比例約10%，CoreWeave向輝達採購GPU，再把算力對外出租給包括Meta這類超大型科技企業在內的各類客戶。
paras_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that CoreWeave’s financial situation is improving and that Nvidia has no need to provide additional support. Until recently, the credit market had turned negative on CoreWeave, seeing its default risk rising sharply and the probability exceeding 50%. Nvidia is CoreWeave’s second‑largest shareholder, holding about 10% of the company.
Huang told an audience in Stockholm, Sweden on Thursday the 15th, “I’m optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually going down.” He is trying to boost confidence in the data‑center operator.

CoreWeave is an important test case for whether a wave of emerging‑business models can succeed. These firms have sprung up to meet what Nvidia and others describe as an almost limitless demand for AI compute power.

Companies like CoreWeave have taken on large amounts of debt with backing from suppliers such as Nvidia, sparking market concerns about “circular financing” and the possibility that this model creates artificial demand.

In January this year, Nvidia announced a deepened partnership with CoreWeave that includes a $2 billion investment from Nvidia, while CoreWeave pledged to build data centers with more than 5 GW of compute capacity using Nvidia technology by 2030.

Nvidia currently holds 47.2 million CoreWeave shares, roughly a 10% stake. CoreWeave purchases GPUs from Nvidia and then rents the compute capacity to a range of customers, including mega‑tech firms like Meta.

items.title: 多年對手為AI聯手！蘋果攜Meta把大型模型搬上Mac
items.title_en: Longtime Rivals Join Forces for AI! Apple Teams with Meta to Bring Large Model to Mac
paras: 多年對手因AI找到合作契機。蘋果(AAPL-US)與Meta(META-US)周四(15日)宣布攜手，讓開發者能在高階Mac電腦上執行Meta新推出的開放權重模型Muse Spark Open，直接在自己的設備上寫程式、分析影片及執行AI代理任務，不必將模型運算交給雲端。不過，要把這套大型模型搬上桌面，現階段硬體投入超過4萬美元。
綜合外媒報導，這項歷經數月籌備的合作，出現在特納斯(John Ternus)上月接替庫克出任蘋果執行長之後，也反映AI競爭正在改變矽谷長年的合作與對立關係。雙方均未透露，這是否代表未來將展開更深入的合作。

大型AI搬上Mac 開發者不必全靠雲端

Muse Spark Open採用混合專家架構，擁有8,160億個參數，主要針對程式開發與AI代理任務設計。開放權重代表開發者可下載模型參數，在自己的硬體上執行，但仍須遵守授權條件；Meta表示，這款模型允許有限度的商業使用。
為配合合作，蘋果更新MLX機器學習工具，讓模型能跨多台Mac分攤運算，並公布相關技術文件與晶片效能測試。開發者可從Hugging Face等平台下載適用版本，不必再為蘋果晶片額外調整設定，模型也已針對Mac硬體優化執行速度。
Meta AI主管汪滔(Alexandr Wang)表示，許多強大的開放權重模型體積太大，不適合多數個人電腦，但Mac Studio提供的記憶體容量，讓運行Muse Spark Open變得可行。
雙方表示，讓模型直接在使用者設備上運作，可增加資料安全保障，並降低對雲端算力租用的依賴。這也讓開發者在研究、應用程式開發與影片製作上，多了一項美國業者提供的模型選擇。

免租雲端有代價 硬體投入超過4萬美元

要運行這款模型，使用者須串聯2至4台Mac Studio，整組設備合計至少具備1TB記憶體，並非一般單台Mac就能負荷。
目前搭載M5 Ultra晶片與256GB記憶體的Mac Studio，每台售價至少10,799美元；配備512GB記憶體的版本則預定本月稍晚推出。以目前配置計算，整套硬體成本超過4萬美元，入手門檻並不低。
不過，對長期需要大量算力的應用程式開發者或企業而言，租用相近規模的雲端運算資源，每月可能花費數千美元，因此自購設備仍可能隨使用時間拉長而回本，實際效益則取決於使用需求。
Mac的優勢之一，是晶片之間可共用大容量記憶體，搭配MLX串聯多台設備，處理單機難以容納的模型。Meta今年稍早也購買數百台Mac，供超級智慧團隊測試在電腦上執行AI與代理任務。

多年對手找到交集 Meta擴大開放模型布局

蘋果與Meta長年關係緊張，尤其蘋果2021年推出隱私政策變更，限制廣告追蹤能力後，雙方衝突加深。Meta曾估計，這項改變將使其2022年營收減少約100億美元。
汪滔表示，雙方如今找到具有建設性的合作方式，並提到曾任蘋果主管的Meta研究員格羅斯(Daniel Gross)，是促成合作的重要人物之一。
對Meta而言，這也是去年重整AI團隊後，第二款開放權重模型。公司8月先推出較小型的Muse Glimmer，本周稍早則發表專有模型Muse Wonder，持續同時布局開放與封閉模型。
不過，Muse Spark Open並非Meta最先進的產品，能力仍不及Muse Wonder。Meta也承認，中國開放模型在軟體開發及部分其他任務上依然領先。汪滔表示，開放模型將在全球扮演重要角色，美國業者也應參與其中。
他並期待，企業與開發者先以這款模型進行小規模測試，之後再擴大使用。對蘋果而言，這項合作則強化了Mac作為AI開發設備的吸引力，也讓其晶片在大型資料中心之外，找到更多AI運算應用。
paras_en: Longtime rivals have found a cooperation opportunity through AI. Apple (AAPL-US) and Meta (META-US) announced on Thursday (the 15th) that developers can run Meta's newly released open-weight model Muse Spark Open on high‑end Macs, allowing them to write code, analyze video and execute AI agent tasks directly on their own devices without sending model computations to the cloud. However, moving this large model to the desktop currently requires hardware investments of over $40,000.

According to foreign media reports, the months‑long collaboration emerged after John Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as Apple’s CEO last month, reflecting how AI competition is reshaping long‑standing cooperation and rivalry in Silicon Valley. Neither side disclosed whether this signals deeper future collaboration.

Large AI on Mac means developers no longer have to rely entirely on the cloud. Muse Spark Open uses a mixture‑of‑experts architecture with 816 billion parameters, designed primarily for software development and AI‑agent tasks. Open weights mean developers can download the model parameters and run them on their own hardware, subject to licensing terms; Meta says the model permits limited commercial use.

To support the partnership, Apple updated its MLX machine‑learning toolkit so the model can be distributed across multiple Macs, and released related technical documentation and chip performance tests. Developers can download compatible versions from platforms such as Hugging Face without needing extra configuration for Apple silicon, and the model has been optimized for Mac hardware speed.
Meta AI head Alexandr Wang said many powerful open‑weight models are too large for most personal computers, but the memory capacity of Mac Studio makes running Muse Spark Open feasible.

Both parties said running the model directly on the user’s device enhances data security and reduces reliance on rented cloud compute, giving developers in research, app development and video production an additional model option from a U.S. provider.

Avoiding cloud rentals comes at a cost: hardware investment exceeds $40,000. To run the model, users must link 2‑4 Mac Studios, with the entire setup requiring at least 1 TB of memory, which a single Mac cannot handle.

Current Mac Studios equipped with the M5 Ultra chip and 256 GB of memory start at $10,799 each; a 512 GB‑memory version is slated for release later this month. With the present configuration, the total hardware cost tops $40,000, setting a high entry barrier.

However, for developers or enterprises that need sustained high compute over the long term, renting comparable cloud resources can cost several thousand dollars per month, so purchasing equipment may still pay off over time; the actual benefit depends on usage needs.

One advantage of Macs is that their chips can share large memory pools, and when paired with MLX to link multiple devices, they can handle models that a single machine cannot accommodate. Meta earlier this year bought hundreds of Macs for its Super‑Intelligence team to test AI and agent tasks on computers.

Longtime rivals have found common ground as Meta expands its open‑model portfolio. Apple and Meta have had a tense relationship for years, especially after Apple’s 2021 privacy policy changes that limited ad tracking, deepening the conflict. Meta estimated the change would cut its 2022 revenue by about $10 billion.
Wang said the two sides have now found a constructive way to cooperate and mentioned former Apple executive‑turned‑Meta researcher Daniel Gross as a key figure in making the partnership happen.

For Meta, this is the second open‑weight model released after reorganizing its AI team last year. The company launched a smaller Muse Glimmer in August and earlier this week unveiled the proprietary Muse Wonder, continuing to pursue both open and closed models.

Nevertheless, Muse Spark Open is not Meta’s most advanced product and is less capable than Muse Wonder. Meta also acknowledged that Chinese open models still lead in software development and some other tasks. Wang said open models will play an important global role and U.S. companies should participate.

He hopes enterprises and developers will first conduct small‑scale tests with this model before scaling up. For Apple, the partnership strengthens the Mac’s appeal as an AI development platform and gives its chips more AI compute use cases beyond large data centers.

items.title: AI泡沫破了錢往哪跑？美銀點名美債 OpenAI風波已提前預演
items.title_en: Where Does Money Flow When the AI Bubble Bursts? BofA Flags US Treasuries as AI Turmoil Pre‑Played
paras: 美國銀行(BAC-US) 警告，若AI泡沫破裂，市場可能出現美股與美債殖利率同步下跌的走勢，債券重新發揮避險功能。
10月OpenAI上週四(8日)發布營收引發科技股重挫、美債殖利率走低，已被美銀視為「AI交易平倉的最佳預演」，顯示私人AI企業的風險可能透過科技股與信用市場向外擴散。
英國《金融時報》上週四報導，OpenAI年化營收遠低於市場流傳數字，當日那斯達克指數下跌逾1%，費城半導體指數重挫3.4%，美債殖利率也隨之走低。
美銀衍生性商品團隊在《全球股票波動率洞察》報告中指出，關鍵不僅是科技股下跌，而是債市反應出現轉變。過去數月，市場常見股票下跌、殖利率上升，意味股債價格同跌；但這次AI衝擊卻使資金轉向債市避險。
類似走勢在10月14日再次出現。美國消費者物價指數（CPI）高於預期，一度推升10年期美債殖利率，市場預期升息的機率短暫突破50%。
不過，隨著CoreWeave(CRWV-US) 股價暴跌逾15%、信用違約交換（CDS）利差擴大135個基點，殖利率迅速回落，終場接近持平。
15日，10年期美債殖利率進一步下跌10個基點至5.09%，觸及三週低點；同時，MSCI亞太股票指數重挫逾3%，韓股盤中一度暴跌9%，顯示股市賣壓與債市避險需求同步升溫。

AI投資降溫反而有利債券

美銀認為，AI泡沫破裂對債市的影響，不僅來自傳統避險資金流入。AI投資週期降溫，意味資本支出減少、電力與資源需求下降，進而壓抑經濟成長及通膨，為債券提供額外支撐。
這也解釋了為何AI風險升高時，股票與殖利率可能同步下滑。若賣壓源自AI成長前景惡化，債券便有機會重新發揮對沖股票風險的功能。
報告以2000年網路泡沫破裂為例，當時那斯達克100指數崩跌，10年期美債殖利率也從約6.5%降至4%區間中段。美銀坦言，目前兩次事件仍不足以構成完整規律，但歷史經驗與宏觀邏輯已提供參考。

私人AI企業風險傳向那斯達克

美銀分析師Benjamin Bowler、Nitin Saksena及Arjun Goyal等人指出，10月8日那斯達克明顯落後大盤，與2025年1月DeepSeek衝擊，以及今年夏季半導體股回檔時的表現相似。
原因在於那斯達克對私人AI生態的曝險較高。OpenAI、Anthropic等未上市企業一旦出現問題，那斯達克100指數便成為公開市場中率先承壓的代理標的，美銀因此將其列為進行AI多空交易的首選指數。
Anthropic已於10月14日向華爾街開放財務數據，而OpenAI總營收與淨營收之間的200億美元差距仍待釐清，這條由私人企業傳向公開市場的風險路徑，將持續受到考驗。

CoreWeave凸顯信用風險

信用市場則揭示AI泡沫另一條潛在破裂路徑。CoreWeave(CRWV-US) 的2032年到期公司債，相對公債利差突破1,000個基點、殖利率升至15%後，股價單日重挫逾15%，創上市以來第三大跌幅。
DA Davidson分析師Gil Luria將CoreWeave比擬為AI領域的次級房貸風險，指出其融資成本約9%，投資報酬率卻僅約1%，並警告若公司無法償債，股價可能歸零。其CDS價格目前隱含的五年違約機率已達63%。
賣壓也波及其他業者，DigitalOcean(DOCN-US) 下跌14%、Hut 8(HUT-US) 跌10%，Nebius(NBIS-US) 與IREN(IREN-US) 各跌約9%，甲骨文(ORCL-US) 也下挫9%。Gartner預估，80%的新興雲端運算企業將在2030年前停止獨立營運。
本週AI類股表現較標普500非AI成分股落後840個基點。BTIG策略師Jonathan Krinsky認為，當前市場的痛苦交易指向「利率下行、那斯達克下行」；若科技七巨頭也開始出現與半導體股相同的走勢，將進一步印證其「紅色十月」判斷。

美銀以利率條件降低避險成本

針對AI泡沫風險，美銀提出結合那斯達克100賣權與利率條件的避險策略。傳統賣權若買得太早，市場持續上漲後，履約價可能逐漸落後，降低保護效果；「最大回望賣權」則可讓履約價隨市場上漲調高，但成本較高。
美銀因此加入利率觸發條件，須在10年期SOFR利率低於目前遠期利率25個基點時才生效。其2027年9月到期方案，指示性權利金為3.62%，較未附利率條件的回望賣權便宜46%。
這項策略的主要風險，是市場重演2022年情境：通膨衝擊或聯準會意外緊縮，使股票與債券價格同步下跌、殖利率上升，利率條件便可能無法觸發。

泡沫集中局部 波動風險仍升高

美銀泡沫風險指標顯示，目前標普500僅13檔股票讀數超過0.8，合計權重約2.4%，遠低於網路泡沫高峰期的20%至40%，顯示股價泡沫尚未全面擴散。
不過，Jefferies將當前局面形容為「AI的2008時刻」，指出兩家持續消耗現金的AI實驗室，占2.3兆美元未完成訂單的一半，風險可能潛藏於資產負債表。
美銀也提醒，選擇權做市商的避險部位目前仍壓抑市場波動，但若標普500跌破7700點附近，相關緩衝可能快速減弱，使逢低買進轉向「越跌越賣」。
後續生產者物價指數（PPI）、Anthropic財務揭露及大型科技公司財報，將進一步檢驗AI風險向股債市場傳導的程度。
paras_en: Bank of America (BAC-US) warns that if the AI bubble bursts, the market could see a simultaneous decline in US equities and Treasury yields, with bonds regaining their safe‑haven role.

Last Thursday (Oct 8), OpenAI’s revenue release triggered a sharp drop in tech stocks and a dip in Treasury yields, which BofA called the "best rehearsal for AI trade unwind," showing that private‑AI firm risks can spill over to tech equities and credit markets.

The Financial Times reported last Thursday that OpenAI’s annualized revenue was far below market‑circulated figures; the Nasdaq fell more than 1%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 3.4%, and Treasury yields also slipped.

BofA’s derivatives team noted in its Global Equity Volatility Insights report that the key is not just the tech‑stock decline but a shift in bond‑market reaction. In recent months, stock drops usually coincided with rising yields (both falling together), but the AI shock is pushing capital into bonds for safety.
A similar pattern re‑emerged on Oct 14 when US CPI came in hotter than expected, briefly pushing 10‑year Treasury yields up and lifting the probability of a rate hike above 50% for a short spell.
However, as CoreWeave (CRWV-US) tumbled more than 15% and its credit‑default‑swap spread widened by 135 basis points, yields quickly fell back, ending almost flat.

On the 15th, the 10‑year Treasury yield slipped another 10 basis points to 5.09%, hitting a three‑week low, while the MSCI Asia‑Pacific Index dropped over 3% and Korean stocks plunged up to 9% intraday, showing synchronized equity sell‑off and bond‑hedge demand.

AI investment cooling benefits bonds. BofA says a burst in the AI bubble would aid bonds not only through traditional safe‑haven flows but also because a slowdown in AI spending cuts capex, power and resource demand, dampening growth and inflation and giving bonds extra support.
That explains why heightened AI risk can cause stocks and yields to fall together. If selling pressure stems from deteriorating AI growth prospects, bonds can once again hedge equity risk.

The report cites the 2000 internet‑bubble burst as an example: the Nasdaq‑100 crashed while 10‑year Treasury yields fell from around 6.5% to the mid‑4% range. BofA admits two events are insufficient to form a firm rule, but history and macro logic offer guidance.

Private‑AI firm risk spreads to the Nasdaq. BofA analysts Benjamin Bowler, Nitin Saksena and Arjun Goyal note that on Oct 8 the Nasdaq lagged the broader market, resembling the DeepSeek shock of Jan 2025 and the summer‑semester semiconductor pullback this year.

The reason is the Nasdaq’s higher exposure to private‑AI ecosystems. If private, unlisted firms like OpenAI or Anthropic encounter trouble, the Nasdaq‑100 becomes the first public‑market proxy to feel pressure, making it BofA’s preferred index for AI long‑short trades.

Anthropic opened its financials to Wall Street on Oct 14, while a $20 billion gap between OpenAI’s total and net revenue remains unresolved; this private‑to‑public risk channel will continue to be tested.

CoreWeave highlights credit risk. Its 2032 corporate bond spread over Treasuries surged past 1,000 basis points, pushing the yield to 15%; the stock fell more than 15% in one day, the third‑largest drop since listing.

DA Davidson analyst Gil Luria likens CoreWeave to sub‑prime mortgage risk in AI, noting financing costs near 9% versus a roughly 1% return, warning that a default could wipe the stock out. Its CDS now implies a five‑year default probability of 63%.

The sell‑off spread to peers: DigitalOcean (DOCN-US) down 14%, Hut 8 (HUT-US) 10%, Nebius (NBIS-US) and IREN (IREN-US) each about 9%, and Oracle (ORCL-US) also fell 9%. Gartner forecasts 80% of emerging cloud firms will cease independent operations by 2030.

AI stocks this week underperformed non‑AI S&P 500 components by 840 basis points. BTIG strategist Jonathan Krinsky says current market pain points to "lower rates, lower Nasdaq"; if the seven big techs start mirroring semiconductor stocks, it would further confirm his "Red October" view.

BofA proposes a hedge that combines Nasdaq‑100 puts with rate‑trigger conditions to lower hedging costs. Traditional puts bought too early can lose effectiveness if the market keeps rising; a "maximum‑lookback" put lets the strike rise with the market but costs more.

Thus BofA adds a rate trigger: the hedge only activates when the 10‑year SOFR rate falls at least 25 basis points below the current forward rate. The September 2027 expiry version carries an indicative premium of 3.62%, 46% cheaper than an unconditioned look‑back put.

The main risk of this strategy is a repeat of the 2022 scenario: an inflation shock or an unexpected Fed tightening causing stocks and bonds to fall together while yields rise, potentially preventing the rate trigger from being met.

BofA’s bubble‑risk gauge shows only 13 S&P 500 stocks have a reading above 0.8, representing about 2.4% of weight—far below the 20‑40% seen at the peak of the internet bubble—indicating the equity bubble has not fully spread yet.

However, Jefferies calls the current situation "AI’s 2008 moment," noting two cash‑burning AI labs together account for half of the $2.3 trillion of unfilled orders, a risk that may be hidden on balance sheets.

BofA also warns that options market‑maker hedges are still dampening volatility, but if the S&P 500 slips below roughly 7,700 points, that buffer could evaporate quickly, turning buying the dip into "sell‑more‑as‑it‑falls" behavior.
Upcoming PPI data, Anthropic’s financial disclosures and big‑tech earnings will further test how far AI risk transmits to equity and bond markets.

items.title: 韓股血洗、台股開始鬆動 亞洲科技股「去槓桿賣壓」引爆全面恐慌
items.title_en: South Korean Stocks Plummet, Taiwan Stocks Start to Waver as Asian Tech Stock “De‑leveraging Sell‑off” Sparks Full‑Scale Panic
paras: 亞洲科技股拋售潮正演變為更廣泛的恐慌。南韓綜合指數(KOSPI) 單日重挫7.6%，跌破長期支撐，先前抗跌的台股也開始回落。隨著AI資本支出前景遭質疑、多頭部位過度集中，市場擔憂去槓桿賣壓擴散，美國半導體股也面臨補跌風險。
韓股跌勢已進入加速階段。南韓綜合指數(KOSPI) 單日下跌7.6%，不僅跌破長期支撐趨勢線，指數也已遠低於200日均線，顯示這波賣壓對長期走勢造成明顯衝擊。
韓股重挫7.6% 超賣程度創多年極值
根據The Market Ear數據，KOSPI目前超賣程度為2022年10月以來最極端水準。當時，韓股在多數全球投資人尚未將目光轉向這個市場前，就已率先觸底。不過，如今即使超賣訊號浮現，賣盤仍未見停歇。
從技術面觀察，今年7月下旬的拋售曾在略低於目前指數的位置獲得支撐，該區域因此被視為眼前最後一道防線。一旦失守，韓股進一步下跌的空間恐將擴大。
波動率走勢也反映市場情緒惡化。先前韓股上漲時，KOSPI隱含波動率便同步攀升，呈現「股價漲、波動率也漲」的異常現象，暗示市場內部結構已出現扭曲。如今股價轉為急跌，波動率卻進一步飆升，市場由上漲階段的異常波動，轉入恐慌性拋售。
韓美走勢分歧 美股補跌疑慮升溫
韓股崩跌之際，KOSPI與美國費城半導體指數（SOX）(SOX) 的表現差距持續擴大。即使費半本身也已回檔，兩者的分歧仍未收斂，反而來到極端水準，成為市場關注的另一項風險。
這道差距將如何縮小，目前存在兩種看法。一種認為韓股已過度下跌，隨著走勢回歸均值，可能迎來反彈；另一種則認為，美國半導體股尚未充分反映下行風險，後續恐承受補跌壓力。
兩種情境目前都有支持者，關鍵在於韓股能否止穩，以及美國半導體股能否維持相對強勢。原文分析認為，隨著市場愈來愈質疑AI資本支出的可持續性，美國半導體股跟進下跌的風險正在上升。
因此，韓股急跌所引發的擔憂，已超出單一市場表現。當AI相關交易的部位仍然擁擠，韓美股市之間的落差，也使投資人更加關注賣壓是否會向其他半導體市場擴散。
**台股抗跌優勢鬆動 AI交易承壓**
先前台股憑藉在AI供應鏈中的核心地位，在亞洲科技股拋售潮中維持相對韌性，與韓股形成明顯落差。然而，這種看似對跌勢「免疫」的狀態，如今也開始動搖。
The Market Ear指出，台股已出現明顯回落跡象，使市場重新檢視台韓股市之間的巨大表現差距能否持續。原本相對抗跌的市場開始鬆動，也加深投資人對AI相關交易可能出現更大範圍調整的疑慮。
台韓股市差距最終是透過韓股反彈，還是台股補跌來收斂，目前仍無定論。不過，台股可能跟進下跌的風險，已開始被市場重新定價，成為這輪拋售接下來的重要觀察焦點。
從持股部位來看，台股AI相關交易的多頭部位仍處於歷史高檔，使市場對短期下跌衝擊格外敏感。當大量資金集中押注同一投資主題，即使長期前景尚未改變，短期賣壓仍可能對股價造成明顯衝擊。
與此同時，通膨疑慮、AI資本支出前景的不確定性，以及中國競爭對手持續崛起，也正形成多重壓力，使台股AI相關資產面臨更嚴格的市場檢驗。
多頭部位擁擠 去槓桿風險擴大
這波亞洲科技股拋售，反映市場正重新評估AI投資主題。過去一年多，大量資金湧入半導體及相關科技股，形成高度擁擠的多頭部位；如今支撐行情的預期出現裂痕，資金撤出的壓力也隨之浮現。
在部位集中的情況下，一旦市場信心動搖，去槓桿速度往往可能超出預期。韓股此次急跌，正凸顯擁擠交易在賣壓湧現時的脆弱性，也使投資人開始擔心類似壓力會否在其他市場重演。
The Market Ear指出，台股AI相關資產的長期投資邏輯或許依然成立，但在多頭部位極度擁擠、市場預期已被大幅推高之際，短期下跌風險仍不容忽視，戰術性下行避險的吸引力正顯著上升。
眼前市場面對的問題，已不只是AI長期成長故事能否延續，更在於短期拋售將如何傳導。從韓股跌破支撐、韓美半導體走勢分歧，到台股抗跌優勢開始鬆動，投資人的關注焦點正轉向：下一個承受集中賣壓的市場會是誰。
paras_en: The sell‑off in Asian technology stocks is turning into a broader panic. South Korea's composite index (KOSPI) plunged 7.6% in a single day, breaking long‑term support, and Taiwan's previously resilient market is now also slipping. With doubts over AI capital‑expenditure outlooks and overly concentrated long positions, markets fear de‑leveraging pressure spreading, while U.S. semiconductor shares face the risk of further declines.

South Korean equities have entered an acceleration phase. The KOSPI fell 7.6% in one day, not only breaking its long‑term trend line but also sinking far below the 200‑day moving average, showing that this wave of selling is markedly impacting the long‑term trajectory.
South Korean stocks tumble 7.6%, creating an oversold level not seen in years

According to data from The Market Ear, the KOSPI’s oversold condition is at its most extreme since October 2022. Back then, Korean shares hit a bottom before most global investors turned their attention to the market. Yet today, even as the oversold signal emerges, selling shows no sign of pausing.

From a technical perspective, a sell‑off in late July found support just below today’s index level, making that zone the last immediate barrier. If it breaks, the downside space for Korean equities could widen considerably.

Volatility trends also mirror deteriorating sentiment. When Korean stocks were rising, KOSPI implied volatility rose in tandem, an unusual “price up, volatility up” pattern that hinted at internal market distortion. Now prices are crashing while volatility spikes even higher, shifting the market from abnormal volatility in an up‑trend to panic‑driven selling.
Divergence Between Korea and the U.S. Raises Concerns of Further U.S. Pull‑backs

As Korean stocks collapse, the performance gap between the KOSPI and the U.S. Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) continues to widen. Even though the SOX has already pulled back, the divergence remains extreme, becoming another focal risk for investors.

Two views explain how the gap might narrow. One sees Korean equities as oversold, expecting a mean‑reversion bounce; the other argues U.S. semiconductor stocks have not yet fully priced in downside risk and may face further pull‑backs.

Both scenarios have supporters. The key question is whether Korean stocks can stabilise and whether U.S. semiconductor shares can maintain relative strength. The original analysis notes that growing scepticism about the sustainability of AI capital spending is raising the risk of a follow‑on decline in U.S. semiconductor stocks.

Thus, the anxiety triggered by the Korean sell‑off extends beyond a single market. With AI‑related positions still crowded, the widening gap between Korean and U.S. markets makes investors increasingly wary that selling pressure could spill into other semiconductor markets.
Taiwan’s Defensive Edge Erodes as AI Trades Come Under Strain

Previously, Taiwan’s market leveraged its core role in the AI supply chain to stay relatively resilient amid the Asian tech sell‑off, creating a clear contrast with Korean stocks. That apparent immunity to declines is now beginning to wobble.

The Market Ear notes that Taiwan’s market is showing clear signs of retreat, prompting a reassessment of whether the large performance gap between Taiwan and Korea can persist. The once‑defensive stance is loosening, deepening concerns that AI‑related trades could face a broader correction.

It remains uncertain whether the Taiwan‑Korea gap will close via a Korean rebound or a Taiwanese pull‑back. However, the risk of Taiwan following the sell‑off is already being re‑priced, becoming a key focus for the next phase of the market decline.

From a holdings perspective, long positions in AI‑related Taiwanese stocks remain at historic highs, making the market especially sensitive to short‑term downside shocks. When large sums of capital are concentrated on a single theme, even unchanged long‑term fundamentals can still allow short‑term selling to hit prices hard.

At the same time, inflation worries, uncertainty over AI capital‑expenditure prospects, and the continued rise of Chinese competitors are creating multiple pressures that put Taiwan’s AI‑related assets under stricter market scrutiny.
Crowded Long Positions Amplify De‑leveraging Risks

This wave of Asian tech stock selling reflects a market re‑evaluating the AI investment theme. Over the past year, massive inflows into semiconductor and related tech stocks created highly crowded long positions; now cracks in the expectations that supported the rally are exposing withdrawal pressure.

When positions are concentrated, a loss of confidence can accelerate de‑leveraging beyond expectations. The sharp Korean drop highlights the fragility of crowded trades when sell‑off pressure emerges, and investors are now fearing similar stress could repeat in other markets.

The Market Ear points out that the long‑term investment logic for Taiwan’s AI‑related assets may still hold, but with extremely crowded longs and expectations pushed far higher, short‑term downside risk cannot be ignored, and tactical hedging is becoming markedly more attractive.

The current market issue is no longer just whether the long‑term AI growth story can continue, but how short‑term selling will propagate. From Korean support breaks and Korea‑U.S. semiconductor divergence to Taiwan’s waning defensive edge, investors’ focus is shifting to: which market will be the next to bear concentrated selling pressure.

items.title: CoreWeave股債雙殺！黃仁勳出面力挺：不需要輝達紓困
items.title_en: CoreWeave Stock and Bond Double Hit! Jensen Huang Steps In to Back the Company: No Need for Nvidia Rescue
paras: CoreWeave(CRWV-US)股債雙殺、債務違約疑慮升溫，輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳出面力挺這家重要客戶，表示公司實力持續改善，並不認為CoreWeave需要輝達出手紓困。他的談話也帶動CoreWeave周四(15日)盤中股價收復部分跌幅。
據《彭博》報導，黃仁勳在斯德哥爾摩一場活動上受訪時表示：「CoreWeave的實力每天都在改善。我很樂觀，他們的資金成本實際上正在下降。」
這番安撫市場的談話，正值信用市場投資人日益擔憂CoreWeave可能陷入財務危機。這家AI資料中心營運商，是觀察新興AI算力供應商商業模式能否持續的重要案例。CoreWeave等業者在輝達等供應商協助下大舉舉債，也引發市場質疑，這類循環融資是否創造了不實需求。
輝達不僅是CoreWeave的重要供應商，也是其第二大股東，持股約10%，讓兩家公司的關係格外受到關注。
CoreWeave股價周三重挫15%，周四盤中一度再跌9.5%，在黃仁勳發言後收復部分失土。債市同樣承受賣壓，公司2032年到期債券，四個月前投資人仍以面額買進，周三報價已跌至每1美元面額約剩0.78美元。馬斯克也在旗下社群平台針對這項跌勢回應「哎呀」(yikes)。
投資人為CoreWeave債務購買違約保障的成本也急升。根據ICE Data Services資料，其5年期信用違約交換(CDS)利差一度擴大74.5個基點至1,194.5個基點，創盤中歷史新高，市場報價隱含未來5年違約機率超過六成。這是衍生性商品價格反映的風險評估，並非違約已成定局。
儘管CoreWeave營收加速成長，規模仍遠不及龐大債務。華爾街預估，公司今年營收將達129億美元，明年還將成長逾一倍；但其債務已超過400億美元，其中相當大一部分將在未來5年內到期。
沉重的債務支出持續消耗現金，自由現金流的負值也愈來愈大。根據市場估計，CoreWeave今年虧損將擴大至逾25億美元。
CoreWeave的財務疑慮也成為本周全球股市賣壓的推力之一。投資人擔心，AI基礎設施建設規模已超出企業取得投資回報的能力，後續可能面臨投資縮減。費城半導體指數本周以來已下跌逾9%，反映市場對AI擴張與融資風險的戒心升高。
paras_en: CoreWeave (CRWV-US) suffered a double blow to its equity and debt, raising concerns of a possible default, and Nvidia (NVDA-US) CEO Jensen Huang stepped in to back this key customer, saying the company’s fundamentals are improving and he does not believe CoreWeave needs a rescue from Nvidia. His comments helped CoreWeave recover part of its losses during Thursday’s (the 15th) intraday trading.
According to Bloomberg, Huang told reporters at an event in Stockholm, “CoreWeave’s strength is improving every day. I’m optimistic – their cost of capital is actually going down.”

The reassuring remarks come as credit‑market investors grow increasingly worried that CoreWeave could slide into a financial crisis. The AI data‑center operator is a litmus test for whether emerging AI‑compute providers can sustain their business models. Companies like CoreWeave have taken on large amounts of debt with the help of suppliers such as Nvidia, prompting market scepticism about whether this circular financing creates artificial demand.
Nvidia is not only a major supplier to CoreWeave but also its second‑largest shareholder, owning roughly 10% of the company, which puts extra focus on the relationship between the two firms.

CoreWeave’s shares plunged 15% on Wednesday and fell another 9.5% during Thursday’s session before recouping some ground after Huang’s remarks. The bond market was also hit, with the company’s 2032 notes—bought at par just four months ago—trading around $0.78 on the dollar on Wednesday. Elon Musk even reacted on his platform with a “yikes.”

The cost for investors to buy default protection on CoreWeave’s debt surged sharply. ICE Data Services showed the five‑year credit‑default swap spread spike to 1,194.5 basis points, up 74.5 points, a record high for the session and implying a more than 60% chance of default over the next five years. This reflects market‑perceived risk, not a certain default.

Even though CoreWeave’s revenue is accelerating, its scale remains far below its massive debt load. Wall Street estimates the company will generate $12.9 billion in revenue this year and more than double that next year, but its debt exceeds $40 billion, with a sizable portion maturing within the next five years.
Heavy debt service continues to drain cash, and negative free cash flow is widening. Market estimates project CoreWeave’s loss this year to expand to over $2.5 billion.

The financial worries surrounding CoreWeave have become one of the drivers of global equity sell‑offs this week. Investors fear that the scale of AI infrastructure build‑out has outstripped companies’ ability to earn a return on investment, potentially leading to a pull‑back in spending. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has fallen more than 9% this week, reflecting heightened caution about AI expansion and financing risks.

items.title: 每天至少10通電話追產能！AI大廠搶台積電 擴張計畫恐受限
items.title_en: At Least 10 Calls a Day to Chase Capacity! AI Giants Vie for TSMC, Expansion Plans May Be Constrained
paras: AI大廠為了搶台積電產能，電話一通接一通。台積電(2330-TW)(TSM-US)北美執行長達拉爾(Sajiv Dalal)向《CNBC》透露，他每天至少接到10通詢問晶圓產能的電話。隨著晶片業者與科技巨頭加碼AI投資，先進製程供給能否跟上需求，正成為牽動整個產業擴張的關鍵。
台積電周四(15日)公布獲利連續第六季創新高，並預期第四季營收年增58%，凸顯先進晶片需求強勁。不過，比財報數字更值得關注的是，客戶對產能的需求仍超過供應能力。瑞穗證券分析師克萊恩(Jordan Klein)形容，競爭「極為激烈」，各家公司都在設法爭取更多議價籌碼與供應量。

巨頭新創都來搶產能 合作關係成關鍵

台積電承接輝達(NVDA-US)、超微(AMD-US)與博通(AVGO-US)等業者的先進晶片製造需求，蘋果(AAPL-US)、Alphabet(GOOGL-US)旗下Google、亞馬遜(AMZN-US)、微軟(MSFT-US)、Meta(META-US)及OpenAI，也仰賴台積電生產自研AI加速器。
克萊恩警告，若未來12至18個月運算需求維持目前增速，台積電的產能限制可能威脅部分大型基礎設施投資，以及AI公司的積極營收成長目標。美國超大規模雲端業者今年資本支出預估遠超過7,000億美元，分析師預期2027年還會進一步增加。
除了全球記憶體短缺，先進邏輯晶片的製造也構成挑戰。這類晶片生產複雜、成本高昂，輝達與超微等業者往往提前數年，私下與台積電洽談長期合約及客製化安排。黃仁勳與蘇姿丰今年也都多次訪台。
對訂單規模較小的新創而言，長期合作關係尤其重要。AI晶片新創D-Matrix執行長謝斯(Sid Sheth)表示，自己與台積電往來逾20年，台積電資深副總經理張曉強(Kevin Zhang)則是客戶爭取產能的關鍵人物。他打趣形容，張曉強「現在可能是全世界最受歡迎的人」。
D-Matrix製造副總裁庫拜恩(Jerry Qubain)自1992年起便拜訪台積電，目前每年赴台3至4次。謝斯表示，公司2024年延攬他，正是看重他與台積電的深厚關係。
台積電2025年共有534家客戶，前十大客戶貢獻78%淨營收，前兩大分別占19%與17%。儘管新創得與巨頭競爭，謝斯認為，台積電仍有動機支持潛力新秀，就像早年扶植輝達與博通，期待培養未來的大客戶。

擴產需要時間 第二供應來源浮上檯面

台積電正加快在台灣、日本與美國亞利桑那州擴產。今年7月，公司宣布追加1,000億美元投資，在亞利桑那原規劃的六座晶圓廠之外再增建數座，總承諾金額達2,650億美元，並傳出評估在德州設立新廠。
然而，新產能需要數年才能到位。分析師指出，台積電也透過在既有廠房增設艾司摩爾(ASML-US)極紫外光(EUV)微影設備等方式提高產能。艾司摩爾周三公布財報時表示，客戶已對安排至2030年的訂單表達興趣。
供給吃緊也替三星電子(005930-KR)與英特爾(INTC-US)創造機會。TechInsights分析師哈奇森(Dan Hutcheson)表示，客戶希望取得第二供應來源，以增加與台積電議價的籌碼。
儘管英特爾晶圓代工業務多年來面臨延誤與挫折，哈奇森指出，大型晶片業者如今都在英特爾進行測試。不過，測試能否轉化為量產訂單，仍是後續觀察重點。
隨著台積電擴大美國布局，客戶爭取晶圓產能的競爭又持續升溫，克萊恩認為，台積電已成為全球戰略地位最有利的企業之一。
paras_en: AI giants are calling nonstop to snag TSMC capacity. TSMC (2330‑TW)(TSM‑US) North America CEO Sajiv Dalal told CNBC he receives at least ten phone calls a day asking about wafer capacity. As chip makers and tech behemoths pour more money into AI, whether advanced‑process supply can keep up with demand is becoming the key factor shaping the industry’s expansion.

TSMC announced on Thursday (the 15th) that its profit hit a record high for the sixth consecutive quarter and it expects fourth‑quarter revenue to grow 58% year‑over‑year, underscoring strong demand for advanced chips. Yet more telling than the numbers is that customer demand still outstrips supply. Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein described the competition as “extremely fierce,” with every company scrambling for more bargaining power and supply volume.

Both tech giants and startups are racing for capacity, making partnerships crucial. TSMC is handling advanced‑chip manufacturing orders from Nvidia (NVDA‑US), AMD (AMD‑US) and Broadcom (AVGO‑US), while Apple (AAPL‑US), Alphabet’s Google, Amazon (AMZN‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US), Meta (META‑US) and OpenAI also rely on TSMC to produce their in‑house AI accelerators.

Klein warned that if compute demand stays on its current growth path for the next 12‑18 months, TSMC’s capacity constraints could jeopardize some large‑scale infrastructure investments and AI companies’ aggressive revenue‑growth targets. U.S. hyperscale cloud providers are projected to spend well over $700 billion on capex this year, with analysts expecting the figure to rise further by 2027.

In addition to a global memory shortage, manufacturing advanced logic chips is a major challenge. These chips are complex and costly to produce, so companies like Nvidia and AMD often negotiate long‑term contracts and custom arrangements with TSMC years in advance. Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and AMD’s Lisa Su both visited Taiwan multiple times this year.

For smaller‑scale startups, long‑term relationships are especially important. AI‑chip startup D‑Matrix CEO Sid Sheth said he has dealt with TSMC for over 20 years, and senior VP Kevin Zhang is the key person customers rely on to secure capacity. Sheth joked that Zhang is “probably the most popular person in the world right now.”

D‑Matrix manufacturing VP Jerry Qubain has been visiting TSMC since 1992 and now travels to Taiwan three to four times a year. Sheth noted the company hired him in 2024 precisely because of his deep ties with TSMC.

TSMC will have 534 customers in 2025, with its top ten accounting for 78% of net revenue and the top two alone contributing 19% and 17%. Although startups must compete with giants, Sheth believes TSMC still has an incentive to back promising newcomers, just as it once nurtured Nvidia and Broadcom, hoping to grow future big customers.

Capacity expansion takes time, and a second source is emerging. TSMC is accelerating expansion in Taiwan, Japan and Arizona, USA. In July the company announced an additional $100 billion investment, adding several new fabs to the six originally planned in Arizona, bringing total commitments to $265 billion, and it is reportedly evaluating a new plant in Texas.

However, new capacity will not be ready for years. Analysts note TSMC is also boosting output by installing more ASML (ASML‑US) extreme‑ultraviolet (EUV) lithography tools in existing fabs. ASML said on Wednesday that customers have already shown interest in orders scheduled through 2030.

Tight supply is also creating opportunities for Samsung Electronics (005930‑KR) and Intel (INTC‑US). TechInsights analyst Dan Hutcheson said customers want a second source to increase their leverage against TSMC.

Although Intel’s foundry business has faced delays and setbacks for years, Hutcheson pointed out that large chip makers are now testing at Intel. Whether those tests turn into volume orders remains to be seen.
As TSMC expands its U.S. footprint, competition among customers for wafer capacity continues to heat up. Klein believes TSMC has become one of the most strategically advantaged companies worldwide.

供給吃緊也替三星電子(005930-KR)與英特爾(INTC-US)創造機會。TechInsights分析師哈奇森(Dan Hutcheson)表示，客戶希望取得第二供應來源，以增加與台積電議價的籌碼。
儘管英特爾晶圓代工業務多年來面臨延誤與挫折，哈奇森指出，大型晶片業者如今都在英特爾進行測試。不過，測試能否轉化為量產訂單，仍是後續觀察重點。
隨著台積電擴大美國布局，客戶爭取晶圓產能的競爭又持續升溫，克萊恩認為，台積電已成為全球戰略地位最有利的企業之一。
paras_en: AI giants are calling nonstop to snag TSMC capacity. TSMC (2330‑TW)(TSM‑US) North America CEO Sajiv Dalal told CNBC he receives at least ten phone calls a day asking about wafer capacity. As chip makers and tech behemoths pour more money into AI, whether advanced‑process supply can keep up with demand is becoming the key factor shaping the industry’s expansion.

TSMC announced on Thursday (the 15th) that its profit hit a record high for the sixth consecutive quarter and it expects fourth‑quarter revenue to grow 58% year‑over‑year, underscoring strong demand for advanced chips. Yet more telling than the numbers is that customer demand still outstrips supply. Mizuho analyst Jordan Klein described the competition as “extremely fierce,” with every company scrambling for more bargaining power and supply volume.

Both tech giants and startups are racing for capacity, making partnerships crucial. TSMC is handling advanced‑chip manufacturing orders from Nvidia (NVDA‑US), AMD (AMD‑US) and Broadcom (AVGO‑US), while Apple (AAPL‑US), Alphabet’s Google, Amazon (AMZN‑US), Microsoft (MSFT‑US), Meta (META‑US) and OpenAI also rely on TSMC to produce their in‑house AI accelerators.

Klein warned that if compute demand stays on its current growth path for the next 12‑18 months, TSMC’s capacity constraints could jeopardize some large‑scale infrastructure investments and AI companies’ aggressive revenue‑growth targets. U.S. hyperscale cloud providers are projected to spend well over $700 billion on capex this year, with analysts expecting the figure to rise further by 2027.

In addition to a global memory shortage, manufacturing advanced logic chips is a major challenge. These chips are complex and costly to produce, so companies like Nvidia and AMD often negotiate long‑term contracts and custom arrangements with TSMC years in advance. Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and AMD’s Lisa Su both visited Taiwan multiple times this year.

For smaller‑scale startups, long‑term relationships are especially important. AI‑chip startup D‑Matrix CEO Sid Sheth said he has dealt with TSMC for over 20 years, and senior VP Kevin Zhang is the key person customers rely on to secure capacity. Sheth joked that Zhang is “probably the most popular person in the world right now.”

D‑Matrix manufacturing VP Jerry Qubain has been visiting TSMC since 1992 and now travels to Taiwan three to four times a year. Sheth noted the company hired him in 2024 precisely because of his deep ties with TSMC.

TSMC will have 534 customers in 2025, with its top ten accounting for 78% of net revenue and the top two alone contributing 19% and 17%. Although startups must compete with giants, Sheth believes TSMC still has an incentive to back promising newcomers, just as it once nurtured Nvidia and Broadcom, hoping to grow future big customers.

Capacity expansion takes time, and a second source is emerging. TSMC is accelerating expansion in Taiwan, Japan and Arizona, USA. In July the company announced an additional $100 billion investment, adding several new fabs to the six originally planned in Arizona, bringing total commitments to $265 billion, and it is reportedly evaluating a new plant in Texas.

However, new capacity will not be ready for years. Analysts note TSMC is also boosting output by installing more ASML (ASML‑US) extreme‑ultraviolet (EUV) lithography tools in existing fabs. ASML said on Wednesday that customers have already shown interest in orders scheduled through 2030.

Tight supply is also creating opportunities for Samsung Electronics (005930‑KR) and Intel (INTC‑US). TechInsights analyst Dan Hutcheson said customers want a second source to increase their leverage against TSMC.

Although Intel’s foundry business has faced delays and setbacks for years, Hutcheson pointed out that large chip makers are now testing at Intel. Whether those tests turn into volume orders remains to be seen.
As TSMC expands its U.S. footprint, competition among customers for wafer capacity continues to heat up. Klein believes TSMC has become one of the most strategically advantaged companies worldwide.

paras: 美國CPI高於預期，台股今(15)日面臨大賣壓，外資出重手創史上最大賣超，「第四法人」以一當十，資金湧入市值雙雄元大台灣50(0050-TW)、元大台灣50正2(00631L-TW)，單日淨申購分別獲378億元、119億元，其中0050更創下歷史新高，穩居投資人低接最佳標的。
15日外資賣超3,025億台股重挫，點燃內資進場火力，15日ETF成交金額排行榜前五名全數衝破百億元。市值型雙雄0050、00631L，單日成交金額分別高達495.3億與244.1億元，穩坐冠、亞軍。
資金申購動能同樣驚人，0050單日淨申購378億元改寫新高，00631L亦獲119億元，創下半年來單日最大申購量，顯見「成熟投資人」無畏外資調節持股，看好台股長期成長與反彈契機，把握低檔分批布局。
法人分析，資金青睞重點關鍵在於反彈力道，00631L追求台灣50指數正向2倍績效，反彈力道更是強勁，統計史上五大單日跌幅包括2025/4對等關稅、2024/8日圓升值、2018/10美中貿易戰，以及2020/3全球疫情，後六個月漲幅達24.3%至147.3%、後一年漲幅達40.5%至314.9%，後續反彈動能備受期待。
觀察投資人逆勢加碼標的，統計10月以來0050已5度、00631L已3度單日成交金額突破百億。台灣50指數聚焦台灣核心企業，在產業競爭力與資金集中效應下，長期下來有著領先大盤的優勢。統計近十年，台灣50指數含息報酬率為961.75%，大幅優於加權報酬指數的751.92%。
法人進一步分析，近年ETF興盛，資金優先透過0050、00631L等市值型ETF買進權值股，形成「資金集中、標的集中」第四法人之力，強力為台股護航，加上「護國神山」台積電最新法說會公布第三季營收、獲利雙創新高，董事長魏哲家更信心喊話「台積電獲利能力沒上限」，為市場下一波反彈上攻行情，再祭一劑強心針。

paras_en: U.S. CPI came in higher than expected, and the Taiwan market faced heavy selling pressure on the 15th. Foreign investors dumped a record‑size net amount, while the “fourth institutional investors” acted like ten times the size, pouring money into the two market‑cap giants Yuanta Taiwan 50 (0050‑TW) and Yuanta Taiwan 50 Leveraged 2x (00631L‑TW). They logged net subscriptions of NT$37.8 billion and NT$11.9 billion respectively in a single day, with 0050 hitting an all‑time high and remaining the top pick for investors seeking a low‑entry, high‑potential target.

On the 15th, foreign investors sold NT$302.5 billion worth of Taiwan stocks, triggering a sharp rebound from domestic capital. All five of the day’s top ETF turnover rankings exceeded NT$10 billion. The market‑cap leaders 0050 and 00631L posted daily transaction values of NT$49.53 billion and NT$24.41 billion respectively, securing first and second place.

The subscription momentum was equally striking: 0050’s net daily subscription of NT$37.8 billion set a new record, while 00631L attracted NT$11.9 billion, the largest single‑day inflow of the half‑year. This shows that “mature investors” are undeterred by foreign‑owned share adjustments, remain bullish on Taiwan’s long‑term growth and rebound opportunities, and are building positions at lower levels in batches.

Analysts note that investors favor these funds because of their rebound potential. 00631L seeks to deliver twice the positive performance of the Taiwan 50 index, and its rebound strength is robust. Historically, the five largest single‑day declines occurred in April 2025 (tariff parity), August 2024 (yen appreciation), October 2018 (U.S.–China trade war), and March 2020 (global pandemic). In the six months following those drops, gains reached 24.3 % to 147.3 %; in the subsequent year, gains rose 40.5 % to 314.9 %, fueling expectations of further rebound momentum.

Observing investors’ contrarian additions, data show that since October, 0050 has exceeded NT$10 billion in daily turnover five times, and 00631L three times. The Taiwan 50 index concentrates on Taiwan’s core enterprises; under industry competitiveness and capital concentration, it enjoys a long‑term advantage over the broader market. Over the past ten years, the Taiwan 50 index’s total return (including dividends) was 961.75 %, far outperforming the weighted index’s 751.92 %.

Further analysis points out that the recent ETF boom has led capital to prioritize market‑cap ETFs such as 0050 and 00631L to buy heavyweight stocks, creating a “concentrated‑capital, concentrated‑target” force of the fourth institutional investors that strongly supports the Taiwan market. Coupled with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s latest earnings call announcing record‑high Q3 revenue and profit, Chairman Wei Zhe‑Jia’s confident claim that “TSMC’s profit‑making capacity has no ceiling” provides an additional boost for the next market rebound.
